rubrics_metrics.name: Truthfulness: keep strictly in the domain of truth (writing natural history)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fabre asserts: 'while keeping strictly in the domain of truth, I avoid your scientific prose' — the writer must tell the exact narrative of facts observed, neither more nor less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Natural-history writing should present accurate observations and not invent or embellish facts; the author defends lively prose while insisting on factual accuracy (Preface).

rubrics_metrics.name: Write to make young readers love natural history
rubrics_metrics.description: Fabre: 'I write above all for the young. I want to make them love the natural history which you make them hate.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The aim of retelling is to inspire affection and curiosity in young readers; style choices should prioritize engagement and accessibility (Preface).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid tedious or excessively technical scientific prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Fabre recounts criticism that his books are 'too interesting' and contrasts his engaging style with the 'scientific prose' of some colleagues which he says 'seems borrowed from some Iroquois idiom.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor clear, readable language over dry, formulaic technical exposition when addressing non-specialist or young audiences (Preface).

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe living creatures in their life and context rather than only dissecting them
rubrics_metrics.description: Fabre contrasts studying 'alive' under the sky and observing instinct and life with dissecting work: 'you pry into death, I pry into life... I study instinct in its loftiest manifestations.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field observation and behavioral study are recommended methods for natural-history writing and teaching (Preface).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patience and careful recording in observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Fabre emphasizes 'the patience with which I observe you, of the care with which I record your actions' as the basis for truthful narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality natural-history accounts rely on prolonged, careful observation and meticulous recording of behavior and facts (Preface).

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplify and retell for young audiences without sacrificing truth
rubrics_metrics.description: The book is 'Retold for Young People'—the implicit rule is to simplify language and presentation for children while remaining truthful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt content to the comprehension and interests of young readers, preserving factual accuracy and observational integrity (Title page, Preface context).
